pr_body: #### Checklist - [x] run `npm run test` and `npm run benchmark` - [x] tests and/or benchmarks are included - [x] documentation is changed or added - [x] commit message and code follows [Code of conduct](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/master/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) Closes: #703 `sandbox.js` will be removed when this feature is finished. It is a useful file for testing during development. I think I have to move `toString.js` into `lib` as well. Some things to note: - This is a very simple implementation of the full toString method - I'd like to print the Plugins and Middleware for each route in a similar format to `fastify.printRoutes` but I'm not sure where to start with that as that method is coming from `find-my-way`. (Should I try to copy that function and edit it to fit our needs?) - How should the `json` output be structured?
pr_comments: Oh great! Thanks for the tip. How do access the routes on a Fastify instance? Do I need to access it through `find-my-way`?

`find-my-way` does not exposes the registered path, @mcollina had a similar problem in [fastify/fastify-routes-stats](https://github.com/fastify/fastify-routes-stats).
At the moment the only way to access the declared route url is by using the `onRoute` hook.
But since this is a feature implemented directly in core you can access the [`routes`](https://github.com/delvedor/find-my-way/blob/master/index.js#L36) property of the router.

Are Plugins tracked on the Fastify instance? AFAIK most plugins just decorate the instance (or the request/reply parts of the instance) and that is it. I wonder whats the best way to show that back to the user. -- Could this require editing `.decorate` and make it start storing the names or references to the new functions?

@Ethan-Arrowood yes I think so. However we are loosing all these metadata about fastify after boot finishes. However, I would add all these stuff in steps, and this is a good one.

You might want to add some events/or metadata info to https://github.com/mcollina/avvio as plugins are tracked there. (The code in avvio is __very__ complex).
Hello! I just got back from a 2 week trip and I'll be continuing work on this feature soon.
@mcollina can you provide some insight into adding events/or metadata info to avvio?
I would emit an event when a plugin start loading, and when a plugin finishes loading. However, there will be a to ton (every route is wrapped in a plugin) so some filtering might be needed.
This needs unit tests.

Not to worry about the delay. I've been quite busy myself. Thank you for the review. I'll make sure to fix these things soon, but can you please review my previous comment on this thread regarding `pluginUtils.registeredPlugins`? Once that is figure out I can start polishing this up. Thank you!

The `registeredPlugins` only track names. Basically that array tells which plugins have been loaded in the current tree, but it does not represent the tree itself at the root. See https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/953616f565585406f6e923d55883eda979eb6776/fastify.js#L397.

I think you can extend that mechanism to track down the tree of loaded plugins, without touching avvio at all.
Okay interesting. I'll mess around with that a bit more and see what I can make of it.

(branch has been rebased properly)
@mcollina / @delvedor I noticed that `fastify` was never actually tracking plugins. I've updated the `.register` method to now do so but had to use a weird work around with `avvio`.

The way it works is the `fastify` instance inherits the `.use` method from `avvio` and assigns it to `fastify.register`. Then it declares its own `.use` method (for registering middleware). But in order to track plugins being added I needed to expand the `fastify.register` command to push the added plugin to `fastify[pluginUtils.registeredPlugins]`. Let me know if you see a better way to do this.

Also I didn't know what we should do about anonymously named plugins so I added two things:
1. A warning that users should name their plugins
2. The toString method concatenates the string `'anonymous'` with the index of the plugin and adds that to the output string.

You can check out this behavior by running the included `sandbox.js` file. 

If you think the `toString` method is at a good place I can work on unit tests next.

I'm not able to get the linter to successfully run. Not sure what I broke or what I'm doing wrong but this is my console output: It is the same output when I run `npm run lint` or `npm run test` Any idea whats going on here? - I've deleted `node_modules` - Ran `npm install` - I'm using node 10.4.0 and npm 6.1.0 Made this into a proper issue (#968)
Tests are passing on cloud, so it looks like a problem on your side.
It's failing on appveyor: https://ci.appveyor.com/project/mcollina/fastify/build/1.0.1715/job/eq4v8m6k66i01b28

It is coming from `fastify-plugin` again. Hmm I can't seem to reproduce this locally (i loaded up node 9.11.1 and all unit tests pass fine). Could appveyor not be using the up-to-date fastify-plugin maybe?

(Maybe you just initiated this but) Greenkeeper just initialized a chore(package) to update `fastify-plugin` to v1.1.1 Once that completes I think we need to re run the build on this pr and it should pass.
@mcollina @delvedor is there anything I can do to get this merged?
Travis CI failed on Node 9. Console log says it was a stalled build? I guess it needs to be restarted; not sure why it would fail on Node 9 and not 6, 8, or 10

@Ethan-Arrowood all seems in order now (CI is green)!

@fastify/fastify are you good with this?

I've restarted the CI, now is all good!
I'll review this asap! :)

@nwoltman okay I've implemented your recommendations. Code is a lot cleaner now. 

After looking at this and how `fastify-plugin` handles meta data I'm wondering if it would be better to make a change in `fastify-plugin`. I think that instead of declaring a new property on the plugin object:

https://github.com/fastify/fastify-plugin/blob/2f0cf764eb80f152395fac15dded2baa0359d183/index.js#L15

We use the `checkName` method and update the `options.name` object instead. This of course would prioritize an existing `options.name` value, but if that value doesn't exist, then `fastify-plugin` will set it automatically. Fastify will then push every registered plugin to the `registered-plugins` array and there will be no need for this `Symbol.for('fastify.display-name')` thing.

Let me know what you think about this. If you want I can code this and make the appropriate pr over on `fastify-plugin`.
@Ethan-Arrowood That sounds like a good idea. Storing the plugin's name in a single place keeps things nice and simple 👍

@nwoltman by adding this feature to `fastify-plugin`, all functions returned from `fp` will contain a meta prop object. Is this okay? There is currently a line in `fastify-plugin` that simply returns the `fn` if no `options` object is passed. Similarly, if a `string` is passed to the `options` parameter, it is treated as a version check and also **does not** attach the `Symbol.for('plugin-meta')` options object. 

I'm going to open a PR on the fastify-plugin repo with my proposed changes so you can see the new behavior via the code.

@Ethan-Arrowood I think that should be alright. The `plugin-meta` symbol property is not a documented API and changing it so that the property always exists doesn't break any code in this repo. To be safe, we might want to consider it as a semver-major change for the `fastify-plugin` package, but I'm not sure if we really need to.
@nwoltman are you ok for landing this after https://github.com/fastify/fastify-plugin/pull/44 is landed?

@mcollina There are still some changes that will need to be made to this PR once fastify/fastify-plugin#44 lands, such as updating the documentation and using `meta.name` instead of the `fastify.display-name` symbol.

`fastify-plugin` is ready to get merged and then this pr requires a dependency update + some minor code updates and will be good to go.

https://github.com/fastify/fastify-plugin/pull/44#issuecomment-401602758
@Ethan-Arrowood fastify-plugin 1.2.0 is out.
@nwoltman if we go with that plan, then we need to document `plugin-meta` somewhere. fastify-plugin is a mere utility and it should be possible to do the same things _without_ it.
@mcollina You're right. Using `fastify-plugin` shouldn't be a requirement to naming a plugin.

Nested hooks were intentionally left out as of right now. Looking back on your original issue I see how we may want to display this information. 

So per your example the expected out put might look like something like this?
```
Hooks: []
├── /
│
├── hello (GET)
│
└── v1/ 
    │   Hooks: [preHandler]
    │
    ├── hello (GET) 
    │
    └── inside/hello (GET)
        └── Hooks: [preHandler]
```

If this is what you want it to be instead of what it currently is then this feature will need quite a bit more work (which I'm okay with doing). I do not know how Fastify exposes these things internally so I cannot gauge how difficult this change will be.

@Ethan-Arrowood yes, kind of:
```
Hooks: []
Middlewares: []
├── /
├── hello (GET)
│
└── v1/ 
│   │   Hooks: [preHandler]
│   │   Middlewares: []
│   ├── hello (GET) 
│   ├── status/check (HEAD) 
│   │
│   └── inside/
│       │   Hooks: [preHandler]
│       │   Middlewares: []
│       ├── hello (GET) 
│       └── hello/update (POST)
│
└── v2/ 
    │   Hooks: [preHandler, onSend]
    │   Middlewares: []
    ├── hello (GET) 
    └── status/check (HEAD) 
```

I think we can drop the use of `printRoutes` and build our own method. We might want to use [node-archy](https://github.com/substack/node-archy) to build the tree.
It's definitely not an easy task, but we will give you support everywhere we can!

Probably a nice solution could be add an internal event emitter which emits an event for every route/hook/middleware/plugin registered with its own context. If you want I can work on it :)
Thank you for the recommendations. I think I'll take on the challenge and see how far I can go on my own. I'll make sure to ping here if i need help!

issue_context.title: Feature: toString method
issue_context.body:
As discussed in #702 could be a nice feature expose a `toString` method.
It should print the routes, the decorators/hooks/middlewares for every encapsulation level as well as custom error handlers and not found handlers.

I think it could be an amazing feature, extremely useful for debugging and see the "size" and complexity of your application visually.
@fastify/fastify what do you think?

Example:
```
 Hooks: [authHook, compressHook]
├── /
│
├── test (GET)
│   │    Plugins: [cookie-plugin]
│   └── /hello (GET)
│
│   Plugins: [point-of-view, fastify-postgres]
│   Custom handlers: [500handler]
└── hello/world (GET)
```

Thanks to the `onRoute` hook I think it could even be a plugin.
comments:
Also mentioned was adding a custom `util.inspect` method. So might as well round off the set and add https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Symbol/toStringTag.

I'd really like to see `.toJSON` added at the same time. While the described `.toString` behavior would be fine for debug purposes, I can guarantee you that someone will end up using it in production. Therefore, providing a mechanism to accomplish the same thing for production logging would head off some issues.
+1 for `.toJSON`, I expect it to be more useful for developers.
I like this idea and interested in working on it.
Fantastic!
What are the properties that need to be printed? Should this be its own plugin or can I add this to fastify core?

I think it would be good to have it in fastify itself, because we are likely not keeping track of all the info atm.

We should print:

1. plugins
2. hooks registered for every lifecycle phase
3. routes
4. middlewares (ideally)
Spent some time on this today. Not complete yet but I think its a good start. Check out my notes on the PR for more details and maybe we can continue the implementation discussion over there.

Hello, in spirit of the upcoming JS Interactive conference and hacktoberfest i'd like to try and finish what I started here. Can someone bring me up to speed on current expectations for this feature? 

#861 is very much behind master (100 something commits). Is it worth trying to rebase that branch, or should I start a new one and cherry pick any relevant commits over?

Hello! I think rebasing looks fine and will save you some time. Only `package.json` is in conflict. Try and see if it works.

For expectations, others will know better :)
Good point @cemremengu 😄

I'm not 100% convinced about this feature, IMHO it falls in the "nice to have but a nightmare to maintain" section.

@fastify/fastify thoughts?
My opinion posted at the top of this thread has not changed.
@delvedor mentioned using `node-archy` to revamp how `find-my-way` pretty prints routes. Maybe that would be a more worthwhile contribution?

@Ethan-Arrowood `find-my-way` internals will probably change a lot in the future.
I'm not sure if supporting `prettyPrint` will be feasible.
I really prefer having a JSON representation that I can format any way I desire.
Having a `toJSON()` method could also reduce the amount of maintenance needed because then a `toString()` method could be implemented in a plugin.

Okay so it seems like a `toJSON()` method would be better than `toString()`. And I think someone said it before; the information from `toJSON()` could be used in a `toString()` implementation (plugin or not) too.

Should I go forward with this?

I created a branch to try this [feature](https://github.com/Eomm/fastify/commit/7d69c22f029a825a0e53c0e6f2753b76f4572ccd)

The output of the example is the plugins tree:

```
bound root 12 ms

```

But hooks, decorator, and routes are not traced, we should try with all the hooks and the new `onRegister`.
I think this would be way better than our current situation. Adding the routes would be even better.
